<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par37" />{{GHGpar-heading|37|The Interrogative and Indefinite Pronouns}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|37|a}}
'''1.''' The interrogative pronoun is {{GHGheb|text=מִי|translate=who?}} (of persons, even before plurals, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=18|verse=35}}, and sometimes also of things {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=5}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=בַּת־מִי|translate=whose daughter?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=לְמִי|translate=to whom?}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־מִי|translate=whom?}})—{{GHGheb|text=מָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַה}} (see b) ''what?'' (of things).—{{GHGheb|text=אֵי־זֶה|translate=which? what?}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|37|b}}
The form {{GHGheb|text=מַה{{זונג}}ּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַ‍{{זונג}}ּ}}, &c. (followed by ''Dageš forte conjunct.'': even in {{GHGheb|text=יְ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=1}}, &c., against {{GHGpar|20|m}}) may be explained (like the art. {{GHGheb|text=הַ{{זונג}}ּ}} {{GHGpar|35|l}}, and {{GHGheb|text=וַ{{זונג}}ּ}} in the ''imperf. consec.'') from the rapid utterance of the interrogative in connexion with the following word. Most probably, however, the {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}} is rather due to the assimilation of an originally audible {{GHGheb|text=ה}} ({{GHGheb|text=מַהּ}}, as Olshausen), which goes back through the intermediate forms ''math, mat'' to an original ''mant'': so W. Wright, {{GHGcite|title=Comparative Grammar}}, Cambridge, 1890, p. 124, partly following Böttcher, {{GHGcite|title=Hebräische Grammatik}}, § 261. A ground-form ''mant'' would most easily explain {{GHGheb|text=מָן}} (''what?''), used in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=15}} in explanation of {{GHGheb|text=מָן|translate=manna}}, while {{GHGheb|text=מַן}} is the regular Aramaic for ''who''. Socin calls attention to the Arabic ''mah'' (in pause with an audible ''h'': ''Mufaṣṣal'', 193, 8). Observe further that—

{{GHGmargin-letter|37|c}}
(''a'') In the closest connexion, by means of {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַה־}} takes a following {{GHGterm|Dageš}} ({{GHGpar|20|d}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מַה־לָּךְ|translate=what is it to thee?}} and even in ''one'' word, as {{GHGheb|text=מַלָּכֶם|translate=what is it to you?}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=15}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=1|verse=13}}, and even before a guttural, {{GHGheb|text=מהם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=8|verse=6}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|37|d}}
(''b'') Before gutturals in close connexion, by means of {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} or (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=1}}) a conjunctive accent, either {{GHGheb|text=מַה}} is used with a virtual strengthening of the guttural ({{GHGpar|22|c}}), so especially before {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, and, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=36}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=21}}, before {{GHGheb|text=ח}}—or the doubling is wholly omitted. In the latter case either (cf. {{GHGpar|35|e}}–k) ''ă'' is fully lengthened to ''Qames'' (so always before the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} of the article, except in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=2|verse=12}}; also before {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫נָּה}}, and so {{GHGheb|text=ה}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=18}}), {{GHGheb|text=א}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=14}}), {{GHGheb|text=ע}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=13}}), or modified to {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, especially before {{GHGheb|text=עָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=חָ}}, and generally before {{GHGheb|text=הָ}}. The omission of the strengthening also takes place as a rule with {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, {{GHGheb|text=ח}}, {{GHGheb|text=ע}}, when they have not {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}, and then the form is either {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} or {{GHGheb|text=מֶה}}, the latter especially before {{GHGheb|text=ח}} or {{GHGheb|text=ע}}, if {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} follows.

{{GHGmargin-letter|37|e}}
The longer forms {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=מֶה}} are also used ({{GHGheb|text=מֶה}} even before letters which are not gutturals) when not connected by {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} but only by a ''conjunctive accent''. As a rule {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} is then used, but sometimes {{GHGheb|text=מֶה}} when at a greater distance from the principal tone of the sentence, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=4|verse=3}}. (On {{GHGheb|text=מֶה}} in the combinations {{GHGheb|text=כַּמֶּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּמֶּה}}, and even {{GHGheb|text=לָ֫מֶה}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=8}}, cf. {{GHGpar|102|k}} and l.)

{{GHGmargin-letter|37|f}}
(''c'') In the principal pause {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} is used without exception; also as a rule with the smaller ''disjunctives'', and almost always before gutturals ({{GHGheb|text=מֶה}} only in very few cases). On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=מֶה}} more often stands before letters which are not gutturals, when at a greater distance from the principal tone of the sentence, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=1|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=1|verse=9}} (see Köhler on the passage), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=10|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=21}}; cf., however, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=31|verse=2}}, and Delitzsch on the passage.

{{GHGmargin-letter|37|g}}
'''2.''' On {{GHGheb|text=מִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} as indefinite pronouns in the sense of ''quicunque, quodcunque'', and as relatives, ''is qui, id quod'', &c., see {{GHGpar|137|c}}.<section end="par37" /><noinclude>
